thread:
Ava: quick sec check — PR #7243 updates sidecar token TTL to 2h to reduce reauth flaps. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/7243. Planning to merge today ~16:00 PT if no issues.

Jordan: quick glance: changing TTL isn't a secret leak itself, but it increases the window for a leaked token to be useful. Why 2h? any retry/backoff changes? :eyes:

Riley: we saw 5xx/429s on scale-up where all sidecars reauth around the same time. Bumping to 2h reduces churn. We can also add jitter + exponential backoff on refresh.

Jordan: prefer jitter/backoff + keep TTL 1h, or use projected short-lived tokens. If you must keep 2h, limit token scope and add audit logging for refreshes.

Ava: can do. Proposal: scope token to read-only for serving (+no write ops), add audit events, and set local cache jitter. Which is lower-risk vs operational burden?

Morgan: for rollout: schedule a 1-hour canary in us-west-2 before global. If canary looks good, proceed with 10% traffic for 2 hrs then full. I can book 17:00 PT slot.

Jordan: Approved with follow-ups: add a security note in the PR describing scope & rotation plan, include config snippet for TTL/jitter, and create a follow-up task to migrate to projected token flow. LGTM :thumbsup:

Ava: Thanks — I'll update PR and schedule canary. @Morgan ping me when slot is confirmed.

Ava: Config snippet I'm adding to the PR:
```yaml
sidecar:
  token_ttl: 2h
  token_scope: "sidecar-read"
  jitter_ms: 300000
``` 

deploy-bot: Canary scheduled for us-west-2 at 17:00 PT — id: canary-20250601-5

Morgan: noted, will watch auth logs and token-refresh error rates. Ping if anything spikes.

Ava: will follow up with PR link and post-canary signal. Thanks all :raised_hands:
